searches_tried: Local comps.py (pipeline and work) on silver choker chain, foxtail, wheat, heavy silver chain, silver rope chain, silver necklace gm, sterling bracelet; Gowans API searches for choker and sterling silver chain gm (past lots with sale_price); one WebSearch for heavy Bali foxtail chains (only retail/eBay asking results, no completed sales); silver spot from gold-api.com. No Armitage lookups. eBay sold listings (Bali/foxtail wheat chain 925, by weight) would settle it, so Chrome is needed. Gowans pays about $2 to $3.7 per gram for plain sterling chains of 20-45g, roughly melt, and up to about $5/g for one 82g necklace. If 925 and 60-90g, expect roughly $130-$300 hammer; if the mark is absent or it is lower grade or plated, much less.
chrome_hint: eBay sold/completed: 'sterling silver Bali wheat foxtail chain necklace heavy 925' (and 'Indian silver chain 8mm foxtail'), note sold price against listed grams
viewing_check: Find and photograph the 925 mark on the clasp or end caps with a loupe. Weigh it if at all possible (or feel the heft against a known 60g object). Check it is not plated or magnetic, check for solder repairs, and measure length and width.
